strategy_title: Changing tile sizes in kernel body without autotune keys regresses
strategy_description: Changing BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N/BLOCK_K inside the kernel body as hardcoded constexpr assignments while keeping @triton.autotune configs as empty Config({}) dicts (only varying num_warps/num_stages) caused a 1.7x slowdown: elapsed cycles increased from 45k to 78k and executed instructions nearly doubled (2.8M → 5.0M). Registers per thread rose from 64 to 80, shared memory per block tripled (16 KB → 49 KB), cutting Block Limit Shared Mem from 9 to 4 and halving theoretical occupancy (50% → 25%). The SharedMemoryConflicts bank conflict count nearly doubled (3.5M → 7.1M wavefronts) because the larger tile shape increased conflicting accesses per wavefront. The root cause is that tile sizes hardcoded in the kernel body are not visible to the autotune search, so the compiler cannot perform per-config register allocation or shared memory optimization — the larger tiles simply increase resource pressure without any compensating benefit.
applicable_when: Kernel has SharedMemoryConflicts rule triggered with >60% wavefront overhead and tile sizes are hardcoded as constexpr in the kernel body rather than as kernel parameters in autotune configs.
do_not_apply_when: Do not increase tile sizes (BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) as hardcoded constexpr assignments inside the kernel body while keeping autotune configs as empty Config({}) dicts. This increases shared memory footprint and register pressure without giving the compiler visibility to optimize per-config, causing Block Limit Shared Mem to drop, theoretical occupancy to halve, and bank conflict counts to increase proportionally with tile area.
framework_notes: In Triton, tile size constexprs (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) MUST be declared as kernel function parameters (e.g., `BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr` in the function signature) and included as keys in each autotune Config dict. Hardcoding them as local constexpr assignments inside the kernel body while using @triton.autotune only for num_warps/num_stages prevents the compiler from performing per-config register allocation and shared memory optimization, causing resource pressure regressions.
